slides.heading: Next Greater Element
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Stacks
slides.narration: Let's solve Next Greater Element, a medium stacks problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: For each element of a circular array, the next strictly greater value, or -1.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. For each element of a circular array, the next strictly greater value, or -1.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: A monotonic stack holds indices still waiting for a greater value; loop twice for circularity.
slides.narration: A monotonic stack holds indices still waiting for a greater value; loop twice for circularity.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: For each element scan forward (wrapping) → O(n²)
Monotonic decreasing stack, two passes for wrap → O(n)
Each index pushed and popped once
slides.narration: Scanning forward from every element is quadratic. A decreasing stack of unresolved indices resolves them as soon as a bigger value appears. Looping twice handles the circular wrap.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Pop indices whose value is smaller and assign the answer
slides.narration: Step by step. First, iterate twice around the array. Second, pop indices whose value is smaller and assign the answer. Third, push the current index.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We fill the output with minus one and loop i to two n, using j equal i mod n. While the top's value is smaller than a of j, pop and set its answer. Push j only in the first pass.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Only push in the first pass
slides.narration: Store indices so you can write the answer. Only push during the first pass.
